paragraphs: In the morning, a mechanic receives a motorcycle with unstable idle, checks the ignition and fuel injection, and identifies the failed part. They disassemble and clean components, replace seals, and adjust the valves. In the afternoon, they check the electronic controls and chain and conduct a road test to confirm there are no unusual noises. They then complete the work order and estimate and return the motorcycle to its owner.

In one sentence: repair and tune motorcycles so they run properly. U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show that about 14,900 motorcycle mechanics were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 15,700 by 2034, a net increase of about 800 jobs, with roughly 1,500 openings per year and a median annual wage of about $47,200 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace motorcycle mechanics, but it will reshape their workflows by assigning repetitive, structured tasks to tools while people focus on judgment, accountability, and creative problem-solving. Routine execution that follows instructions mechanically will lose ground, while mechanics who understand real-world conditions and make sound decisions will become more valuable.
